newsitem.title: USA: Viacom says Blockbuster head resigning.
newsitem.headline: Viacom says Blockbuster head resigning.

text.p: Warning that it expects disappointing results at its Blockbuster Entertainment unit, Viacom Inc. said Tuesday the unit's chairman was resigning and the company will issue a new class of stock to "track" the video rental business as well as to repay debt.
Viacom said Blockbuster Chairman Bill Fields was resigning "by mutual agreement" and a replacement would be named shortly.
The company also warned that Blockbuster's performance during the first quarter was likely to fall 15 percent to 20 percent short of its performance a year ago.
Viacom's stock was battered after the announcement, falling $4.50 to $25.875 on the American Stock Exchange.
The diversified entertainment company, which is headed by Sumner Redstone, bought Blockbuster in 1994.

Viacom said the unit's poor results were brought on by "the inferior quality of video releases in the period" and the short term costs related to its decision to move Blockbuster's headquarters to Dallas from Ft. Lauderdale, Fla.
It said it expected a 15 percent to 20 percent fall in Blockbuster's first quarter earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization compared with the 1996 first quarter.

Viacom said the new stock issue will track the performance of Blockbuster and, while it will make the stock available to the investors in a public offering, Viacom will retain a majority of the shares.

"Issuing a tracking stock will enable us to raise equity capital to reduce our debt, will provide an attractive opportunity for investors interested in Blockbuster and will make it possible for shareholders to better capture the value of all of Viacom's businesses," Redstone said.
"Viacom intends to retain a significant shareholding in the tracking stock, reflecting our continued belief in Blockbuster's prospects."

At the end of 1996 Blockbuster had more than 5,300 domestic and international video stores in 24 countries and about 500 music stores. Its video and music store operations had 1996 revenues of $3.54 billion.
Until a new Blockbuster chief is selected, Blockbuster's operations will report to Redstone and Viacom Deputy Chairman Tom Dooley, Viacom said.
Field said in a statement: "It is clear to me that general retailing is in my blood and it is time for me to return to the industry where I spent my whole career."
Added Redstone: "Together, we made enormous strides in a short period of time and his insights have been ingrained into Blockbuster's operations."
